title: Security Best Practices
description: Protect your app from common vulnerabilities: CSRF, XSS, SQL injection, and more.

slides.title: Django’s Built‑in Security Features 🛡️
slides.content:
Django provides many security protections out of the box when `DEBUG=False`:
- **CSRF protection** – enabled by default for POST forms.
- **XSS protection** – templates auto‑escape variables.
- **SQL injection prevention** – ORM uses parameterized queries.
- **Clickjacking protection** – `X‑Frame‑Options` middleware.
- **SSL/HTTPS** – can enforce with `SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT`.

But you must configure them properly.

slides.title: Security Settings
slides.content:
# settings.py (production)
SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True          # redirect HTTP to HTTPS
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True         # only send session cookie over HTTPS
CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True            # only send CSRF cookie over HTTPS
SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 31536000       # HTTP Strict Transport Security (1 year)
SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS = True
SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD = True
SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF = True   # prevent MIME type sniffing
SECURE_BROWSER_XSS_FILTER = True     # enable XSS filter

# Set a strong SECRET_KEY (via env var)

quizData.question: Which setting ensures that the session cookie is only sent over HTTPS?
quizData.explanation: `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True` makes the session cookie only transmitted over HTTPS.

slides.title: Preventing Common Attacks
slides.content:
**CSRF**: Use `{% csrf_token %}` in all POST forms. For API endpoints, use token authentication.

**XSS**: Always use `|safe` filter only when you trust the content. Django auto‑escapes by default.

**SQL Injection**: Use Django’s ORM; never concatenate user input into raw SQL.

**Clickjacking**: Use `X_FRAME_OPTIONS = 'DENY'` to prevent your site from being embedded in an iframe.

**Directory Traversal**: Don’t allow users to specify file paths directly; use `os.path.basename` or Django’s `FileField` to limit uploads.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Keep dependencies updated

Regularly run `pip list --outdated` and update packages. Security vulnerabilities are often fixed in new releases.
